title: Urban V’s verses with Agnus Dei gifts claim the wax lamb repels lightning, breaks sin, guards childbirth—so these imagelets escape Trent’s ‘no virtue’ class
source_text: XXIX. Urbanus vero Papa V. plane confidebat orationem suam exauditam fuisse, cum ad Imperatorem Graecorum misit tres Agnus Dei, cum hisce versibus, qui sunt in fine capitis jam citati transcripti. Balsamus & munda cera, cum Chrismatis unda Conficiunt Agnum, quod munus do tibi magnum, Fonte velut natum per mystica sanctificatum. Fulgura de sursum depellit, omne malignum Peccatum frangit, ut Christi sanguis, & angit. Praegnans servatur, simul & partus liberatur, Dona defert dignis, virtutem destruit ignis. Portatus munde, de fluctibus eripit unde. Quae cum ita sint, juxta mentem Papae, qui Ecclesiae Romanae caput est, excipiendi sunt illi agni cerei de numero imaginum, quibus Concilium Tridentinum declarat, nullam inesse virtutem, propter quam colendae sint.
pass_a_gloss: But Pope Urban V plainly trusted that his prayer had been heard when he sent three Agnus Dei to the Emperor of the Greeks with these verses, which are transcribed at the end of the chapter already cited. Balsam and clean wax with the wave of Chrism Make the Lamb, which great gift I give you, Born as from a font, sanctified through mysteries. It drives lightning from above, every malign thing; It breaks sin, as Christ’s blood, and chokes it. The pregnant woman is kept, and the birth is freed together… Which things being so, according to the mind of the Pope, who is head of the Roman Church, those wax lambs are to be excepted from the number of images to which the Council of Trent declares no virtue inheres because of which they should be cultivated.
pass_b_english: Urban V’s gift-verses treat the wax Agnus as lightning-ward, sin-breaking, and childbirth-guarding.
On the Pope’s own mind, such imagelets sit outside Trent’s ‘images have no cult-virtue’ rule—or expose its hollow edge.

lemmas.gloss: those wax lambs are to be excepted
